summary: PIDS-Bench evaluates stateless input-level prompt-injection detectors on single input strings labeled as injections or benign. A detector returns a binary decision or a score thresholded to binary. It acts before the input reaches the downstream language model and uses no downstream output. The selected threshold is fixed before application to held-out test and stress sets. Injection examples combine public prompt-injection datasets and template-derived attacks, with source labels accepted without relabeling. Benign inputs combine public corpora and generated benign templates; released benign rows are paraphrase variants that inherit seed labels. The stated evaluation scope is single-turn English-language inputs. The selected methods passages do not establish a row-level language audit or demonstrate that every evaluated item is English. This is a binary input-detection evaluation; downstream attack execution is outside the stated boundary.
gaps: Selected passages do not establish a row-level English-language audit or every evaluated item’s language.
The stated language scope and construction description are source statements, not an independent corpus inspection.
checker_requirement: Separate source checker must assess this draft and release suitability; no provider restriction attestation is made.
